feedback.problem: Let $I=[0,2]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}={i}\times [-i,i].$ Which of the following represents ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the union of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *at least one* set:

$$
{⋃}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for at least one}\,\,k\in I}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=1,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{1}={1}\times [-1,1]={(1,k)\,:\,k\in [-1,1]}.
$$

This represents a vertical line segment from the point $(1,-1)$ to the point $(1,1)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/f26fa8a525806370f5505ad097ead2b289192bb3a6eb3e341eb7c2f91a03531f.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}={i}\times [-i,i]={(i,k)\,:\,k\in [-i,i]}
$$

is the vertical line segment from the point $(i,-i)$ to the point $(i,i).$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/bfeafe4c3b800b33b4f8550de02c2eb908effb5c28ef59b40f8c5e2bcad38ac4.png)

As $i$ runs over $I,$ these line segments sweep the following triangle that represents the union ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/4d860b60ab9e139b26c9f6e1d330188d5e752a51624a2374ad713b6974e66608.png)
